newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker on election/rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker on election/rate worries.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended weaker at C$1.4000 (US$0.7140) on Monday from Friday's close of C$1.3970 (US$0.7158), unsettled by interest rate speculation and Canadian election jitters. * Traders said the currency shrugged off the start of the federal election on Sunday, but weakened after Prime Minister Jean Chretien said he may reverse some planned spending cuts.
Chretien said in a press conference on Monday that he could reverse planned spending cuts in the next fiscal year because of the government's success in cutting its deficit.
"Because we are ahead of schedule on deficit reduction, we can now afford to reinvest in the health care system without jeopardizing our deficit targets," Chretien said.

Chretien pledged to add C$700 million to next year's planned cash transfers under the Canada Health and Social Transfer, the block fund transfer to the provinces. The government had cut transfers from C$19.3 billion in 1994-95 to C$12.5 billion in the current fiscal year.
